# ankra_oidc_trust_policy (Resource)

A GitHub Actions OIDC trust policy: lets workflow runs of one GitHub repository exchange their GitHub ID token (audience `https://ankra.ai/oidc/github`) for a short-lived Ankra token, so CI needs no stored Ankra secret. The counterpart of `ankra org oidc-trust create` and `delete`; a workflow signs in with `ankra login --github-oidc`.

Each policy gets its own service account holding `role_slug`, and every exchange mints a token on that account for at most `ttl_seconds`, narrowed by `scopes` when set. Without `ref`, `environment` or `job_workflow_ref`, any branch, tag, environment and workflow of the repository matches, so pin at least one for anything above `viewer`.

**Who can manage it.** The platform requires the `members.manage` permission on a person's own API token (not a service token, and not a token pinned to a project) and refuses a `role_slug` carrying permissions the token's user does not hold.

**Replacement.** The platform has no update for a trust policy, so changing any argument replaces it: the old policy is deleted and every token it minted is revoked at once, then the new one is created. Destroy does the same. The policy belongs to the organisation, so it needs no provider `project_id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Let the deploy workflow of acme/infra, on main and in the production
# environment, sign in to Ankra with its GitHub OIDC token:
#
#   permissions:
#     id-token: write
#   steps:
#     - run: ankra login --github-oidc --organisation-id <organisation id>
resource "ankra_oidc_trust_policy" "infra_deploy" {
  name                = "infra-deploy"
  repository_owner    = "acme"
  repository_name     = "infra"
  repository_owner_id = 1234567  # gh api users/acme --jq .id
  repository_id       = 89012345 # gh api repos/acme/infra --jq .id
  ref                 = "refs/heads/main"
  environment         = "production"
  role_slug           = "operator"
  ttl_seconds         = 900
}

# A read-only MCP token for an agent workflow, from one reusable workflow.
resource "ankra_oidc_trust_policy" "agents" {
  name                = "agents-mcp"
  repository_owner    = "acme"
  repository_name     = "agents"
  repository_owner_id = 1234567
  repository_id       = 89012399
  job_workflow_ref    = "acme/agents/.github/workflows/agent.yml@refs/heads/main"
  role_slug           = "viewer"
  scopes              = ["mcp:read"]
  ttl_seconds         = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Policy name, unique in the organisation: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, starting with a letter or digit. It also names the policy's service account.
- `repository_id` (Number) GitHub's numeric ID of the repository (`gh api repos/<owner>/<name> --jq .id`). Matching on the ID stops a renamed or re-created repository from inheriting the policy.
- `repository_name` (String) Name of the trusted repository, exactly as GitHub names it.
- `repository_owner` (String) GitHub owner (user or organisation) of the trusted repository, exactly as GitHub names it.
- `repository_owner_id` (Number) GitHub's numeric ID of the repository owner (`gh api users/<owner> --jq .id`). Matching on the ID stops a renamed or re-created owner from inheriting the policy.
- `role_slug` (String) Built-in role the policy's service account holds: `owner`, `admin`, `operator`, `member`, `viewer`. Custom roles are refused, and so is a role carrying permissions the token's user lacks.

### Optional

- `allow_pull_request` (Boolean) Whether runs triggered by `pull_request` events may exchange tokens. Defaults to `false`: a pull request runs code nobody has reviewed yet.
- `environment` (String) Exact GitHub deployment environment the job must run in, such as `production`. Unset matches every environment and jobs without one.
- `job_workflow_ref` (String) Exact `job_workflow_ref` claim the run must carry, such as `acme/infra/.github/workflows/deploy.yml@refs/heads/main`, to trust one (reusable) workflow only. Unset matches every workflow.
- `ref` (String) Exact Git ref a run must be on, such as `refs/heads/main` or `refs/tags/v1.2.3`. No wildcards. Unset matches every ref.
- `scopes` (Set of String) Narrows the minted tokens to these scopes: `mcp:read` and/or `mcp:write` (an MCP-only token). Unset keeps them at the role's full authority; an empty set is refused, because the platform reads it as unset.
- `ttl_seconds` (Number) Lifetime of each minted token, 60 to 3600 seconds. Defaults to 900 (15 minutes).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the policy was created.
- `id` (String) Trust policy ID.
- `service_account_id` (String) ID of the service account the minted tokens belong to.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Trust policies are imported by ID (ankra org oidc-trust list).
terraform import ankra_oidc_trust_policy.infra_deploy 0e0e0e0e-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
